Elena — attaching a marked MSA (first pass) and the draft order form. Two items we need to lock down before legal sign-off:

1) Governing law / seat: CivicAI proposed New York in your first draft. Our legal team usually prefers Delaware for arbitrations but we are open to NY for courts when preserving interim equitable relief. Can you confirm whether CivicAI has a firm position on arbitration seat vs. court seat for emergency relief?

2) Interim/equitable relief carveout: we need clarity whether you can accept a limited carveout that preserves temporary injunctive relief in state/federal courts (to the extent allowed by law) while keeping claims for damages to arbitration. If CivicAI requires full waiver of court access, please flag that now.

3) Service of process / notice: we propose reciprocal service-of-process language with a physical address for each party and an email copy to Legal Ops. Also propose a 48-hour escalation window for emergency contact before filing.

Please see redline for inline suggestions (not exhaustive). Copying Kimberly and David to resolve MSA text. If CivicAI is comfortable, we can offer a short note for the order form that states: "Pending final MSA, parties agree that injunctive relief is available as set forth in the MSA."

Next steps: Elena, can you provide CivicAI's legal point of contact and any non-negotiable jurisdictional requirements by EOD?

Thanks,

— Grace

Grace — thanks for the quick turn. I'm CivicAI's GC for this matter (cc'd). Two quick answers:

1) Governing law: CivicAI's standard is New York law (state courts) for contractual interpretation; arbitration seat is negotiable but we prefer NY as a matter of predictability for enforcement.

2) Interim relief: CivicAI cannot accept language that would permit discovery or damages to go to court outside arbitration, but we will accept a narrow, express carveout allowing either party to seek temporary injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction to prevent imminent and irreparable harm. We want the clause to require the requesting party to notify the other party and attempt to seek expedited arbitration remedies first unless impracticable.

3) Service of process: agree on reciprocal physical addresses plus email to GC. For international service, CivicAI will accept service by email plus courier if the party is outside the U.S.

Attached are CivicAI's suggested snippets (see inline in your redline). Our legal point of contact: Elena Moroz, GC (elena@civicai.com). We can turn around a revised redline by tomorrow morning.

— Elena
General Counsel, CivicAI

Thanks Elena — helpful. A few internal points from Legal Ops and the contract team: 

- If CivicAI accepts a narrow interim relief carveout, we should add a preservation-of-evidence and notice pathway: requesting party must (a) provide notice to the opposing party and to Redwood's legal mailbox (legal@redwood.com) no later than 24 hours after filing; and (b) provide a redacted ex parte summary to enable a quick triage when possible.

- For the seat: Redwood legal accepts New York for court-ordered interim relief but would prefer Delaware for arbitration proceedings. Proposed compromise language we can try: "Governing law: New York. Any claim for damages shall proceed in arbitration seated in Delaware, except that either party may seek temporary injunctive or other provisional relief in state or federal courts located in New York or California."

- Add a short service-of-process block (physical address + email + courier for international).

I've added the above suggestions into the attached redline (see section 13 and 15). David — can you confirm we are okay with the "redacted ex parte summary" approach operationally?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

All — legal has reviewed Kimberly's compromise language and has two suggested edits to tighten enforceability and minimize carveout scope: 

1) Narrow the provisional relief carveout so it explicitly covers "urgent injunctive or other provisional relief necessary to preserve the status quo or prevent imminent, irreparable harm" and excludes discovery or claims for damages.

2) Add an explicit requirement that any party seeking emergency relief must: (i) certify in writing that it provided notice to the other party and legal counsel where practicable; (ii) seek expedited relief from the arbitration provider if available; and (iii) file a status update with both parties' legal reps within 48 hours of filing.

Suggested clause snippet (please treat as redline language):

> Notwithstanding the agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction solely to preserve the status quo or prevent imminent and irreparable harm; such relief shall not include claims for monetary damages, and the party requesting such relief shall, to the extent practicable, (A) provide notice to the other party's legal representative, (B) request expedited relief from the arbitration forum, and (C) notify both parties' legal representatives of any filings within 48 hours.

If CivicAI accepts the above, Legal will clear the MSA with these redlines. Also attaching a short checklist for evidence preservation we use for emergency relief filings (in the drive link).

— David
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
